title: Verbs: the polite present
titleJp: たべます・のみます・します
canDo: I can tell which group a verb belongs to (る, う or irregular) from its dictionary form, and I watch out for the disguised う-verbs (かえる, はいる).
I can put any verb from this lesson into 〜ます (affirmative) and 〜ません (negative).
I can talk about my routine and my plans with the verb at the end: あさ コーヒーを のみます, あした きます.
I can answer a question that has a verb by repeating the verb: はい、〜ます / いいえ、〜ません.

skills: Reading hiragana with some fluency, plus basic katakana (コーヒー, テレビ, テニス).
Sentences with です and the negative じゃないです (lesson 02-3). Here you will see that verbs have their own negative, ません.

The examples use を and に. For now it is enough to know that を marks what is eaten, drunk or watched, and に marks where someone goes. Lesson 03-2 explains each particle in depth: in this lesson, keep your eyes on the verb at the end.

vocab.en: to wake up, to get up (る-verb)
to sleep, to go to bed (る-verb)
to go back home, to return (う-verb disguised as a る-verb)
to enter (う-verb disguised as a る-verb)
to listen, to hear; to ask (う-verb)
to study (irregular: べんきょう + する)

grammar.title: The 3 verb groups
grammar.explanation:
Every Japanese verb has a **dictionary form** — the one you see in vocabulary lists — and it always ends in a **u** sound: たべる, のむ, いく, はなす, する. The verb's **group** decides how it conjugates: the ます form in this lesson and, later on, the て form, the short negative and all the others. So **learn the group together with the meaning**.
• **る-verbs** (called ichidan, 一段, in many sites and videos): they end in る, and the syllable before る has an **e** or **i** sound: たべる (ta-**be**-ru), みる (**mi**-ru), おきる (o-**ki**-ru), ねる (**ne**-ru).
• **う-verbs** (godan, 五段): all the others. They end in う, く, す, つ, ぬ, ぶ, む, ぐ, or in る with an **a, u** or **o** sound before it (わかる, つくる). のむ, いく, はなす, よむ and きく are う-verbs.
• **Irregulars**: only two, **する** (to do) and **くる** (to come). Many verbs are "noun + する" and conjugate the same way: べんきょうする (to study).
• **The disguised ones:** some verbs end in -eru or -iru and are still **う-verbs**. Nothing in the word gives them away; you have to memorize them. The first two to remember: **かえる** (to go back home) and **はいる** (to enter). Others you will meet: はしる (to run), しる (to know).
• **Rule of thumb:** does it not end in る, or end in -aru/-uru/-oru? Then it is **う**, for sure. Does it end in -eru/-iru? Then it is probably **る**, but check the vocabulary list, because it may be a disguised one.
grammar.structure: る: [e/i] + る (たべる, みる) · う: everything else + the disguised ones (かえる, はいる) · irregular: する, くる

examples.jp: マリアさんは パンを たべます。
examples.kana: マリアさんは パンを たべます。
examples.en: Maria eats bread. [たべる is a る-verb: drop る, add ます]

examples.jp: ルーカスさんは うちに かえります。
examples.kana: ルーカスさんは うちに かえります。
examples.en: Lucas goes home. [かえる looks like a る-verb, but it is an う-verb: かえります]

examples.jp: やまださんは あした きます。
examples.kana: やまださんは あした きます。
examples.en: Mr./Ms. Yamada is coming tomorrow. [くる is irregular: きます]

pitfalls: かえる and はいる are disguised う-verbs: かえます ✗ → かえります ✓; はいます ✗ → はいります ✓.
With a る-verb, the whole る goes: みります ✗ → みます ✓.
くる changes its vowel: くります ✗ → きます ✓.
In "noun + する" verbs, only する conjugates: べんきょうます ✗ → べんきょうします ✓.
howToStudy: Make 3 columns in your notebook (る · う · irregular) and sort the 14 verbs from the vocabulary into them. Mark the disguised かえる and はいる with ★.
Speaking: say each verb in its dictionary form and, without pausing, in its ます form (おきる → おきます, かえる → かえります…). Repeat until it comes out without hesitation.
Tap 🔬 on the examples: the ★ PREDICATE block is always the ます verb at the end. Read each sentence starting from it.

grammar.title: 〜ます / 〜ません
grammar.gloss: the polite present: affirmative and negative
grammar.explanation:
〜ます is the **polite** verb ending, at the same level as です: you use it with teachers, classmates and strangers. The negative is **〜ません**. Both attach to the **stem**, the part of the verb that comes before ます.
• **る-verbs:** drop る → たべる → たべ**ます** / たべ**ません**.
• **う-verbs:** the last syllable moves from its **u** sound to the **i** sound in the same kana row, and then ます is added: のむ → の**み**ます, いく → い**き**ます, はなす → はな**し**ます, かう → か**い**ます, まつ → ま**ち**ます, かえる → かえ**り**ます.
• **Irregulars:** する → **します**, くる → **きます**. Negatives: しません, きません.
• **To make it negative**, just swap ます for ません: のみます → のみません. Don't use じゃないです with a verb: that negative is for nouns (lesson 02-3).
• **What the "present" covers:** habits ("I drink coffee in the morning") and the future ("I'll come tomorrow"). It does not cover an action in progress: たべます is "I eat / I will eat", never "I'm eating right now" (lesson 07-1). English "I'm going tomorrow" is a future plan, so あした いきます is right; only "right now, in progress" needs the other form.
• **Questions:** put か at the end (みますか。). To answer, **repeat the verb**: はい、みます。/ いいえ、みません。 — where English says "Yes, I do", Japanese repeats the verb.
• The stem (たべ, のみ, し, き) will come back many times, for example in 〜ませんか (lesson 03-3).
grammar.structure: る: たべる → たべ + ます / ません · う: のむ → のみ + ます / ません (u → i) · する → します · くる → きます

examples.jp: わたしは あさ コーヒーを のみます。
examples.kana: わたしは あさ コーヒーを のみます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa asa kōhī o nomimasu.
examples.en: I drink coffee in the morning. [a habit]

examples.jp: ペドロさんは あした えいがを みません。
examples.kana: ペドロさんは あした えいがを みません。
examples.romaji: Pedoro-san wa ashita eiga o mimasen.
examples.en: Pedro won't watch a movie tomorrow. [future, negative]

examples.jp: しゅうまつ テニスを しますか。— はい、します。
examples.kana: しゅうまつ テニスを しますか。— はい、します。
examples.romaji: Shūmatsu tenisu o shimasu ka. — Hai, shimasu.
examples.en: Do you play tennis on weekends? — Yes, I do.

pitfalls: たべます is not "I'm eating": いま たべます means "I'll eat now". "I'm eating (right now)" uses a different form (lesson 07-1).
With an う-verb, the last syllable changes to its i sound: かくます ✗ → かきます ✓; かうます ✗ → かいます ✓.
Verbs have their own negative: たべるじゃないです ✗ → たべません ✓.
To answer, repeat the verb: みますか。— はい、そうです ✗ → はい、みます ✓. はい、そうです goes with questions about です (lesson 01-1) and is not the natural answer here.
howToStudy: In your notebook, conjugate the 14 verbs from the vocabulary in two columns (ます / ません). Then cover the columns and redo them from memory.
Speaking: ask yourself 5 questions with 〜ますか about your routine and answer them out loud, repeating the verb (はい、〜ます / いいえ、〜ません).

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook, writing the Japanese in kana. Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day.

tasks.prompt: Give the group of each verb (る, う or irregular) and write its 〜ます form.

items.note: き has an i sound before る, and おきる really is a る-verb: drop る, add ます.
It doesn't end in る, so it is definitely an う-verb. す → し.
It looks like a る-verb (e + る), but it is an う-verb. ✗ かえます.
The vowel changes: く → き.
Another disguised one: i + る, but it is an う-verb. ✗ はいます.

items.q: わたしは おちゃを のみます。

a.jp: わたしは おちゃを のみません。

items.q: すずきさんは テレビを みます。

a.jp: すずきさんは テレビを みません。

items.q: アナさんは あした きます。

a.jp: アナさんは あした きません。

items.note: くる → きます → きません.

items.q: わたしは しゅうまつ べんきょうします。

a.jp: わたしは しゅうまつ べんきょうしません。

items.q: たなかさんは うちに かえります。

a.jp: たなかさんは うちに かえりません。

items.note: Swap only ます for ません: the り stays.

tasks.prompt: Translate into Japanese. The verb always goes at the end.

a.jp: わたしは ほんを よみます。
ルーカスさんは コーヒーを のみません。
マリアさんは あした きます。

items.q: Do you listen to music? — Yes, I do.

a.jp: おんがくを ききますか。— はい、ききます。
a.romaji: Ongaku o kikimasu ka. — Hai, kikimasu.

items.note: Answer by repeating the verb, not with そうです.

items.q: Do you play tennis? — No, I don't.

a.jp: テニスを しますか。— いいえ、しません。
a.romaji: Tenisu o shimasu ka. — Iie, shimasen.

items.note: "Play tennis" in Japanese is "do tennis": テニスを します.

a.jp: わたしは うちに かえります。

items.note: かえる is an う-verb: かえります.

tasks.prompt: Write 4 sentences about yourself: 2 about things you do (〜ます) and 2 about things you don't do (〜ません). Use at least one verb from each group. Then read them aloud.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: わたしは あさ パンを たべます。にほんごを べんきょうします。テニスを しません。あした がっこうに いきません。
a.romaji: Watashi wa asa pan o tabemasu. Nihongo o benkyō shimasu. Tenisu o shimasen. Ashita gakkō ni ikimasen.
a.en: I eat bread in the morning. I study Japanese. I don't play tennis. I'm not going to school tomorrow.

items.note: Check: the verb is at the end of every sentence; there is one る-verb (たべる), one う-verb (いく) and one irregular (する); the negative is ません, not じゃないです; わたしは appears only in the first sentence.

workbook.tip: Do it after points 4a and 4b; check it with the official Genki Answer Key.

practice.what: Play normally. Hunt the dialogues for verbs ending in 〜ます or 〜ません: write 5 of them in your notebook and, next to each, its dictionary form and its group (る, う or irregular). If you don't know the dictionary form, put a ? and check the vocabulary list later.
Practice L3 → conjugation. Then the Lesson 3 vocabulary in the SRS.
Journal: write 3 sentences with 〜ません about things you don't do, and use "Anatomy of what I wrote" to check that the verb ended up at the end.
Tap 🔊 on each example in this lesson and repeat along 3 times. Notice that the u in ます is often nearly silent: たべます sounds close to "tabemas".
Record 1 minute describing a typical day using only this lesson's verbs in 〜ます (おきます … たべます … いきます … かえります … ねます). Don't worry about the particles yet.

culture.title: Punctuality: trains on time and arriving early
culture.body: In Japan, **being on time** usually means arriving a few minutes early. For interviews, meetings and classes, people normally arrive about 5 to 10 minutes before the scheduled time. Trains are known for their punctuality: timetables are followed closely, and a delay of just a few minutes often comes with an apology over the loudspeaker. When the delay is long, many railway companies hand out a delay certificate (ちえんしょうめいしょ) that passengers can show at school or work. And if you are going to be late, you are expected to **let people know beforehand**, not just apologize when you arrive.
culture.try: For your next appointment, arrive 5 minutes early. While you wait, say out loud, in Japanese, 3 things you will do afterwards, using this lesson's verbs (うちに かえります、ばんごはんを たべます…).
